explanation:
# Clock tree report: spi_master, clock clk (50 MHz), iteration 1

## Skew
- Skew target (from tool data): 2.0 ns. The spec itself gives no skew target; 2.0 ns is the value in reports/cts_tool.json.
- Worst measured tree skew: 0.007598 ns (max_ss_100C_1v60, hold side), over 9 corners. This is well inside the 2.0 ns target.
- "Tree skew" is the tool's reported skew minus the 0.25 ns clock uncertainty (for example max_ss_100C_1v60 setup: reported 0.256342 ns, uncertainty 0.25 ns, tree skew 0.006342 ns). The reported figures include the uncertainty, so I quote tree skew as the skew of the tree itself.

## Per-corner skew and latency
| Corner | Setup tree skew (ns) | Hold tree skew (ns) | Setup source latency (ns) | Hold source latency (ns) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| max_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.004916 | 0.006269 | 0.250985 | 0.246069 |
| max_ss_100C_1v60 | 0.006342 | 0.007598 | 0.60519 | 0.598827 |
| max_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.005668 | 0.007001 | 0.35698 | 0.351312 |
| min_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.003562 | 0.003897 | 0.239223 | 0.235725 |
| min_ss_100C_1v60 | 0.005242 | 0.005615 | 0.584593 | 0.57935 |
| min_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.004346 | 0.004738 | 0.342255 | 0.337909 |
| nom_ff_n40C_1v95 | 0.004029 | 0.004648 | 0.244615 | 0.240585 |
| nom_ss_100C_1v60 | 0.005798 | 0.00641 | 0.594413 | 0.588466 |
| nom_tt_025C_1v80 | 0.004719 | 0.005327 | 0.349088 | 0.34437 |

Latency is lowest in the ff corners (about 0.24 ns) and highest in the ss corners (about 0.58 to 0.61 ns).

## Clock buffers
- Clock buffers: 9.
- Hold-fix buffers inserted: 79. Timing-repair buffers: 178. These are not clock-tree buffers.

## Effect on hold timing after CTS
Worst hold slack after CTS, only for the three nominal corners the tool reported:
- nom_tt_025C_1v80: 0.301475 ns
- nom_ss_100C_1v60: 0.6181605402523026 ns
- nom_ff_n40C_1v95: 0.013112872270280695 ns (smallest margin)

All three are positive. The ff corner is only about 13 ps above zero, so hold margin there is thin. The tree skew is under 8 ps in every corner, so the clock tree itself adds very little hold stress. The 79 hold buffers show that hold fixing was needed.

Worst setup slack after CTS (same three corners): nom_tt 9.76201 ns, nom_ss 7.035543902160927 ns, nom_ff 9.576872010932588 ns. All positive.

## Not covered
- Hold and setup slack were not given for the max_* and min_* corners, so REQ-021 (every evaluated corner) is not confirmed here. Only the final STA can decide it.
- Transition and clock gating were not in the tool data. The spec (REQ-020) requires no clock gating.
- This report is a read-out of the tool data. I ran no tool and claim no check passed.
assumptions: Tree skew is the tool's reported skew minus the clock uncertainty of 0.25 ns, as given in the tool data.
The 2.0 ns skew target is taken from reports/cts_tool.json because the spec states none.
Hold buffers (79) and timing-repair buffers (178) are reported separately from the 9 clock buffers.
open_issues: Hold slack is thin at nom_ff_n40C_1v95 (0.013112872270280695 ns); needs confirmation in final STA.
Post-CTS slack is given only for the three nominal corners; max_* and min_* corners are not covered for REQ-021.
No clock transition data in the tool output.
